name: Plasma Cell Neoplasms and Spleen Disorders

reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: CRAB (calcium, renal, anaemia, bone) defines active myeloma needing treatment
IgM viscosity without lytic bone means Waldenstrom, not myeloma
Howell Jolly bodies mean absent splenic function with vaccine implications
Ferritin storm plus cytopenias plus haemophagocytosis means HLH emergency
reference.pathophysiology: Clonal plasma cells home to marrow niches secreting monoclonal protein whose light chains obstruct tubules and occasionally misfold into amyloid, while RANKL driven osteoclasts dissolve bone without osteoblast response causing punched lesions and hypercalcaemia. Splenic enlargement mirrors systemic haematological workload or infiltration, and its absence removes marginal zone bacterial clearance.
additionalDifferentials: MGUS versus smouldering versus active myeloma by damage
Myeloma versus Waldenstrom by immunoglobulin class and bone disease
